name: tune-landscape-two-pane
note: Operator decision 2026-10-05 (Nik): in LANDSCAPE on a phone the Tune tab is TWO-PANE for every instrument - tuner (note, cents line, runway, Start/Tone, mode chips) on the left, the string buttons on the right - and the whole thing is usable on ONE screen with NO scroll, including with the mini-player bar up. #366 made the stacked column scroll clear of the bar (the strings were one scroll away); this scenario raises the bar to no scroll at all. Asserts at 915x340, 844x340 and 740x320 (a landscape phone with browser chrome showing) for guitar (6 strings), ukulele (4), banjo (5) and mandolin (4 courses), mini bar up with the video parked: the tuner card and #tStrings sit side by side sharing a band of height; #view scrollHeight <= clientHeight and the tuner card does not scroll internally either; Start, Tone, both mode chips, the runway, the note readout, the cents line and every string are fully on screen, clear of the app bar, tab bar and mini bar, and hit-test to themselves at centre + 4 inner-quarter points (pill chips round off true corners); every control is >=44x44; the strings take the landscape-audit grid (4 strings/courses 2x2, banjo 3+2, guitar 3x2) at 340px tall, including 740x320 (#367 fell back to one row there; inside the landscape rail shell of #369 the header and tab bar are gone, so the grid's rows stay far above the 44px floor and the fallback is retired). Inside the rail shell 'clear of the chrome' means: inside the view box and intersecting neither the .appbar (gear) nor the .tabbar (rail) - the same check that meant 'below the header, above the tab bar' in the old shell. Then 412x800 portrait and 1280x800 desktop keep the stacked column (structural no-regression; exact bounding boxes are diffed against the pre-change build out of band - fonts vary by machine). RED before the change: the 540px stacked column leaves ~110px between the header and the bar, so the view scrolls and the strings sit under the bar.
